articles.title: Armed forces likely to see big-ticket approvals at DAC meet on Thursday
articles.summary: The armed forces are seeking clearance from the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by the Defence Minister, for various defence purchases. These acquisitions, both large and small, aim to bolster India's military capabilities and modernize its equipment. The DAC's approval is crucial for strategic defence procurement, ensuring the forces receive necessary upgrades and systems.

articles.title: Soldier injured in mine blast near LoC in Kashmir
articles.summary: An Indian Army soldier sustained injuries in a landmine blast near the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir's Gulmarg sector on Wednesday. This incident highlights the persistent dangers faced by troops deployed in sensitive border regions, underscoring the constant threat of unexploded ordnance and the challenges of maintaining vigilance along the LoC.

articles.title: Four Astronauts, One Giant Test: What’s at Stake for NASA’s Artemis II Moon Mission
articles.summary: NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule are positioned on Launch Complex 39B, gearing up for the Artemis II mission slated for February 1, 2026. This mission signifies a major advancement in the U.S. space program, aiming to send astronauts further into space than in decades, marking a critical step towards future lunar and deep-space exploration.

articles.title: Pakistan’s Kirana Hills not targeted in Operation Sindoor, IAF struck terror and military sites: Vice Chief Kapoor
articles.summary: During 'Operation Sindoor', the Indian Air Force conducted precise strikes against terror infrastructure and select military installations in Pakistan. Crucially, the IAF deliberately avoided targeting Pakistan's nuclear site at Kirana Hills, as confirmed by the Vice Chief. This operation highlights the IAF's capability for strategic targeting and demonstrates careful restraint, vital aspects for national security and regional stability.

articles.title: India’s bishops elect first Dalit president, demand end to conversion laws
articles.summary: Cardinal Anthony Poola has been elected president of the Catholic Bishops Conference of India (CBCI). This marks a historic milestone as he is the first Dalit, a member of India's historically marginalized castes, to lead the prominent national religious body. His election signifies a significant step towards greater representation and social inclusion within India's institutional framework, reinforcing national unity.

articles.title: Wayne State Head Football Coach Tyrone Wheatley Shocks Team with Announcement
articles.summary: Former NFL player Tyrone Wheatley, a 1995 New York Giants first-round pick, unexpectedly resigned as head coach during the 2026 College Football offseason. His departure surprised his school and team. This development highlights the dynamic nature of coaching careers in competitive sports, where high-pressure environments often lead to significant personnel changes and quick decisions, a trait valuable in any leadership role.

articles.title: Nod to expansion of definition of 'family' for allotment of govt accommodation to service officers
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has approved expanding the definition of "family" for government accommodation allotment to service officers. This decision aims to benefit armed forces personnel by allowing a broader range of dependents to be considered for housing, easing logistical burdens, and enhancing their welfare. It reflects the government's commitment to supporting its servicemen and their families.

articles.title: PM Modi to inaugurate Guwahati–North Guwahati bridge on Feb 14; vehicular movement from March
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the much-awaited Guwahati-North Guwahati bridge during his visit to Assam on February 14. This significant infrastructure project aims to bolster connectivity and facilitate regional development within the state. The inauguration underscores the government's ongoing commitment to enhancing crucial transport networks and driving progress across India, a key aspect of national development.

articles.title: Show HN: I tried to build a soundproof sleep capsule
articles.summary: The article highlights the elusive nature of sound, emphasizing how it leaves no physical evidence like stains or cracks, making its source difficult to pinpoint. It details how an apartment's environment can drastically shift from silent to hostile at night due to pervasive noise, such as bass. This inherent quality of sound poses significant challenges in identifying and addressing noise pollution issues within residential settings.
